title: Category-bar scalar isomorphism as the transpose of the coefficient unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category with identity-cover topology and $\alpha:R\to S$ a homomorphism of commutative rings. Use $R$- and $S$-module presheaves, derived colimits $L_R=L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^R$, $L_S=L\pi_{\mathcal E,!}^S$, exact constant functors $C_R,C_S$, bar complexes $K_R,K_S$ and their canonical derived representatives from [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. Write $T_{\mathcal E}=-\otimes_{\underline R}^{\mathbf L}\underline S$, $T_*=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $r_{\mathcal E},r_*$ for exact scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Give $T_{\mathcal E}\dashv r_{\mathcal E}$ and $T_*\dashv r_*$ the representative-normalized adjunctions of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let $F$ be an $R$-module presheaf and suppose $F[0]$ and $K_R(F)$ are K-flat with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex]; use their canonical tensor comparisons to represent $T_{\mathcal E}F$ by $(F\otimes_R S)[0]$ and $T_*L_RF$ by $Q(K_R(F)\otimes_R S)$.
There is an $S$-linear chain isomorphism, hence an isomorphism in $D(S)$,
$$\Phi_F:K_S(F\otimes_R S)\xrightarrow{\sim}K_R(F)\otimes_R S,\qquad(\sigma,x\otimes s)\longmapsto(\sigma,x)\otimes s,$$
where $\sigma=(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0)$ in degree $-n$. Its inverse sends $(\sum_\sigma(\sigma,x_\sigma))\otimes s$ to $\sum_\sigma(\sigma,x_\sigma\otimes s)$ for finite sums. Let $t_F:F\to r_{\mathcal E}(F\otimes_R S)$ be $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and let $a_F:L_RF\to r_*L_S(F\otimes_R S)$ be its canonical semilinear derived-colimit map, represented by $(\sigma,x)\mapsto(\sigma,x\otimes1)$. The adjunct $\beta_F:T_*L_RF\to L_ST_{\mathcal E}F$ of $a_F$ under $T_*\dashv r_*$ is represented by $\Phi_F^{-1}$. Put $A=L_ST_{\mathcal E}$, $B=T_*L_R$, and $V=r_{\mathcal E}C_S=C_Rr_*$. If $\eta_A:1\to VA$ and $\eta_B:1\to VB$ are the composite units [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], then $V(\beta_F)\eta_{B,F}=\eta_{A,F}$. Thus $\beta_F$ is the component of the unique natural comparison $B\to A$ characterized by this unit equation [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation].

proof.text: Write $H=F\otimes_R S$. Let $\delta_R:1\to C_RL_R$ and $\delta_S:1\to C_SL_S$ be the colimit units. By [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] both are units of the stated derived-colimit adjunctions. Denote the coefficient units by $u_{\mathcal E}$ and $u_*$. By [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], the assumed K-flat, flat-term representatives give $u_{\mathcal E,F}=Q(t_F)$, with $t_F(x)=x\otimes1$, and $u_{*,L_RF}$ is represented on $K_R(F)$ by $z\mapsto z\otimes1$. The same bar theorem represents the canonical semilinear map $a_F$ by $g(\sigma,x)=(\sigma,x\otimes1)$. Every indexing set is small because $\mathcal E$ is small; the displayed direct sums have finite-support elements.

proof.text: For each string $\sigma$, the rule $x\otimes s\mapsto(\sigma,x)\otimes s$ is balanced: $(\sigma,rx)\otimes s=(\sigma,x)\otimes\alpha(r)s$. It therefore extends over each tensor product and then the direct sum to an $S$-linear map $\Phi^{-n}$. In the other direction the rule $(\sum_\sigma(\sigma,x_\sigma),s)\mapsto\sum_\sigma(\sigma,x_\sigma\otimes s)$ is additive in both entries and $R$-balanced; it induces an $S$-linear map $\Psi^{-n}$ out of $K_R(F)^{-n}\otimes_R S$. Both compositions fix the spanning generators $(\sigma,x\otimes s)$ and $(\sigma,x)\otimes s$, respectively. Thus $\Psi^{-n}=(\Phi^{-n})^{-1}$, with exactly the finite-sum formula in the statement. The zero positive-degree terms give the unique zero maps there.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), explicit direct-sum terms; agent tensor-universal-property calculation.

proof.text: Use the faces of [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar]. For $j<n$, both $\Phi d_j$ and $(d_j\otimes1)\Phi$ send $(\sigma,x\otimes s)$ to $(d_j\sigma,x)\otimes s$. For the last face they both give $(d_n\sigma,F(U_1\to U_0)(x))\otimes s$, since the tensor-presheaf restriction is $F(U_1\to U_0)\otimes1$. The signs $(-1)^j$ are the same, so the differentials commute with $\Phi$. Its degreewise inverse $\Psi$ is consequently a chain map as well. This proves the chain isomorphism and, after localization, the asserted isomorphism in $D(S)$. No exactness of tensoring with $S$ is needed for this calculation.

Apply clause (2) of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] on the point site to $P=K_R(F)$, $H^\bullet=K_S(H)$, and $g$ from step 1. Its hypotheses are precisely the assumed K-flatness and flat terms of $K_R(F)$. The adjunct is represented by $z\otimes s\mapsto s g(z)$. On a generator this is $(\sigma,x)\otimes s\mapsto(\sigma,x\otimes s)$, which is $\Psi=\Phi^{-1}$ by step 2. Hence the adjunct $\beta_F$ in the statement is the localized inverse of $\Phi$, using exactly the prescribed tensor comparison, rather than a separately chosen isomorphism.

proof.text:
The canonical semilinear derived-colimit map in [lem-trf-derived-colimit-bar] is formed by transposing the coefficient map followed by the target colimit unit. Unwinding this definition for the identity indexing functor gives $C_R(a_F)\delta_{R,F}=r_{\mathcal E}(\delta_{S,T_{\mathcal E}F})u_{\mathcal E,F}$. Indeed the map to be transposed is $F\xrightarrow{t_F}r_{\mathcal E}H\xrightarrow{r_{\mathcal E}\delta_{S,H}}r_{\mathcal E}C_SL_SH=C_Rr_*L_SH$; its adjoint is $a_F$. This uses the canonical semilinear-map clause of the bar theorem, not just its formula for the complex. By the definition of $\beta_F$ as the coefficient adjunct, $r_*(\beta_F)u_{*,L_RF}=a_F$. Applying $C_R$ and precomposing with $\delta_{R,F}$ therefore gives
$$V(\beta_F)\,C_R(u_{*,L_RF})\delta_{R,F}=r_{\mathcal E}(\delta_{S,T_{\mathcal E}F})u_{\mathcal E,F}.$$
The equality $C_Rr_*=r_{\mathcal E}C_S$ identifies the same underlying constant $R$-complex and the same maps [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], the left inner composite is $\eta_{B,F}$ and the right side is $\eta_{A,F}$. This is the required unit equation.

proof.text: The two composite adjunctions have the same right adjoint $V$ on the whole derived categories. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $L_1=B$, $L_2=A$, and identity right-adjoint isomorphism. It supplies a unique natural isomorphism $c:B\to A$ preserving the units. At $F$, the Hom bijection of $B\dashv V$ is injective and sends a map $b:BF\to AF$ to $V(b)\eta_{B,F}$. Step 5 sends $\beta_F$ to $\eta_{A,F}$, just as $c_F$ does; thus $\beta_F=c_F$. This proves the final natural-comparison assertion even though the explicit K-flat representatives were only assumed for this $F$.
